title: Finite exceptional operations and enriched adjunction on coherent coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $f=pj$ with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-nagata-compactification]. For $W=X,Y$, use the category $\mathscr S_W$ of strict semilinear $((A_n)_W)_n$-module systems, its derived category, reduction functor $\mathcal R_W$, limit functor $\mathcal L_W$, and fiberwise internal and global mapping systems $\mathcal I_W,\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $\mathscr N_W\subset D(\mathscr S_W)$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems whose every level lies in the finite-Tor constructible category $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. No bound independent of $n$ is required.

The finite functors $Rf_{!,n}=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and $Rf_n^!$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] admit functorial realizations $\mathcal F_f:\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$ and $\mathcal E_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$ on these derived coefficient systems. Their evaluations, including quotient maps, are the finite operations and canonical coefficient-change maps. The integral compact-support functor, when defined as the total limit of finite compact supports, is $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ as a functor, with its specified finite projections.

Normalize the coherent dualizing system by $\Omega_W=\mathcal E_{a_W}((A_n)_{\operatorname{Spec}k})_n$ for the structure morphism $a_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the same realization of the finite functors; its level $n$ is $\omega_{W,n}=Ra_{W,n}^!A_n$. Put $\mathcal D_W(M)=\mathcal I_W(M,\Omega_W)$. For $M\in\mathscr N_W$, this dual system belongs to $\mathscr N_W$. Then $\mathcal E_f\cong\mathcal D_Xf^*\mathcal D_Y$ is a natural isomorphism of derived coefficient-system functors, where $f^*$ is derived levelwise finite pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. It is the tensor-Hom evaluation transpose defining the finite dual-formula maps of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], formed on simultaneous system resolutions. It respects normalization and evaluation pairings as identities of system maps. The total limit of the chosen $\Omega_W$ is the dualizing construction of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], with these same finite projections.

For $M\in\mathscr N_X$ and $N\in\mathscr N_Y$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$
$$\mathcal A_{M,N}:\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_fM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(M,\mathcal E_fN).$$
It is the fiberwise derived evaluation/counit transpose on simultaneous coefficient-system resolutions. Its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical finite enriched adjunction
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y,A_n}(Rf_{!,n}M_n,N_n)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(M_n,Rf_n^!N_n),$$
transported from the ordinary etale adjunction by the etale/pro-etale comparison [prop-asd-internal-adjunction, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. This specifies an actual natural transformation before total inverse limit, with its inverse and evaluation/transpose identities, not a lift characterized only by its evaluations. The system comparisons identify the finite units and counits with those of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. No integral exceptional functor, integral adjunction, integral constructibility or Tor bound is asserted.

source.place: Proof, finite dual formula and coefficient adjunction maps; simultaneous coherent refinement is an additional agent-formulated obligation. Resolution foundations: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck). None of these tags alone states the coherent finite exceptional realization.

proof.text: Put $\mathbf C_{W,n}$ equal to the full enhanced subcategory on $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$. For $A=A_m$ and $B=A_n$, the constant $B_W$ is bounded constructible as an $A_W$-module, and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf] gives bounded constructibility and the retained Tor interval for $K\otimes_A^LB$. Tensor associativity gives $(K\otimes_A^LB)\otimes_B^LV\cong K\otimes_A^L\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}V$. The semilinear section theorem identifies normalized systems with cartesian sections and supplies simultaneous models for extension by zero, proper derived direct image, their units, counits, tensor maps, and mates. Thus $\mathcal F_f=Rp_*j_!$ is a functor on normalized systems before any inverse limit, with the stated finite evaluations.

source.place: Coherent refinement of the finite-operation models underlying paragraphs 1-2.

proof.text: Write $\overline X$ for the compactification domain of $p$. It is finite type over $k$, so choose $d\ge0$ with $\dim\overline X\le d$ (and take $d=0$ if empty) by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. If $M_n$ has Tor interval $[a_n,b_n]$, [lem-trf-open-ctf] preserves this interval under $j_!$, and [cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale] gives interval $[a_n,b_n+2d]$ after $p_*$. For $m\ge n$, the normalization map is $Q_YRf_{!,m}M_m\to Rf_{!,n}Q_XM_m\to Rf_{!,n}M_n$; the first arrow is the coefficient comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change], and the second is the normalization of $M$. Both are isomorphisms, with quotient coherences supplied by the simultaneous model in step 1.

source.place: Finite compact-support preservation and coefficient comparison used in paragraph 3.

proof.text: At every finite level, $Rf_n^!$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{!,n}$ on the finite-Tor constructible subcategories, and [thm-sf-preservation-class] keeps this subcategory. Constructible inputs have étale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], while [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identify the finite pro-étale and étale compact-support functors. The finite exceptional statement [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] supplies invertible mates $b_{m,n}$ and identifies their units and counits. Applying [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] therefore defines $\mathcal E_f$ on cartesian sections, with transition $Q_XRf_m^!N_m\xrightarrow{b_{m,n}}Rf_n^!Q_YN_m\to Rf_n^!N_n$; hence it is normalized and levelwise finite-Tor constructible.

source.place: Paragraph 1: finite adjunction; paragraph 3: coefficient mates and their units/counits.

proof.text: For each $W$, choose $d_W\ge0$ with $\dim W\le d_W$ by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] ($W$ is finite type over the field $k$), taking $d_W=0$ when $W$ is empty; this is the dimension hypothesis of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Apply the preceding construction to the structure morphism $a_W$ and the normalized coefficient-unit system. Its normalization is $A_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\cong A_n$, so it gives $\Omega_W=\mathcal E_{a_W}((A_n)_s)_n$ with transitions equal to the counit-defined maps $u_{W,A_m,A_n}$ from [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. The mate construction gives their quotient cocycle, rather than independently chosen evaluations. The value-at-the-unit clause of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] identifies the total limit of this same tower with the prescribed integral dualizing object.

source.place: Paragraph 1: normalization of the finite exceptional tower; last paragraph: value at the structure morphism and coefficient unit.

proof.text: Define $\mathcal D_W(M)=\mathcal I_W(M,\Omega_W)$ using the simultaneous tensor-Hom calculus. Its level is $D_{W,n}M_n$. The finite Verdier preservation and coefficient comparison of [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] and [cor-coef-finite-verdier], transported by [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], show finite-Tor constructibility and invertibility of the normalization map $Q(D_{W,m}M_m)\to D_{W,n}(QM_m)\to D_{W,n}M_n$. The internal-Hom system of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] preserves evaluation pairings and quotient cocycles. Derived pullback acts on the section models by the exact inverse-image clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], using $f^{-1}(A_n)_Y\cong(A_n)_X$. It preserves normalization because exact inverse image commutes with derived coefficient extension: on a K-flat representative $f^{-1}(N_m\otimes_{A_m}A_n)=f^{-1}N_m\otimes_{A_m}A_n$, so the normalization map of $f^*N$ is $f^*$ of that of $N$. Pullback preserves the finite-Tor domain by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], so $\mathcal D_W$ and derived pullback act on $\mathscr N_W$.

source.place: Paragraphs 1 and 3: dual formula and evaluation-preserving duality coefficient change.

proof.text: The compact-support composition comparison for $a_X=a_Yf$ has a simultaneous section model by step 1 and is an isomorphism on evaluations by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Its right-adjoint mate gives $\mathcal E_f\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_X$. For $P=\mathcal D_YN$, [lem-sf-tensor-ctf] and normalization associativity show that $P\otimes N$ and $f^*P\otimes\mathcal E_fN$ lie in the required normalized finite-Tor domains. The projection map from [fix-prop-projection-formula] is invertible at every level, so the same simultaneous model gives an invertible projection comparison.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-3: explicit tensor-Hom/counit construction of the finite dual formula.

proof.text: Transpose $\mathcal F_f(f^*P\otimes\mathcal E_fN)\cong P\otimes\mathcal F_f\mathcal E_fN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_N}P\otimes N$ under the section adjunction, then compose with $\mathcal E_f$ of $P\otimes N\to\Omega_Y$ and with $\mathcal E_f\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_X$. Tensor-Hom transposition produces an actual section map $\theta_N:\mathcal E_fN\to\mathcal D_Xf^*\mathcal D_YN$, formed entirely from the section operations and their counit.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-3: explicit tensor-Hom/counit construction of the finite dual formula.

proof.text:
To prove $\theta_N$ invertible, fix $n$ and pass to the étale site with [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] and the comparisons in steps 3 and 5. The internal-adjunction theorem [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], evaluated at $\omega_Y$ and $\mathcal E_f\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$, gives $Rf_*D_XK\cong D_YF_fK$. For finite-Tor constructible $K$, biduality and ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction yield the natural chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,D_Xf^*D_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*D_YN,D_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YN,Rf_*D_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YN,D_YF_fK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(F_fK,N).$$
The domains are finite-Tor by steps 2 and 5. The final group is $\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\mathcal E_fN)$ by step 3.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-3: explicit tensor-Hom/counit construction of the finite dual formula.

proof.text: Under the displayed bijections, a map $h:K\to\mathcal E_fN$ is sent to the tensor-Hom transpose obtained from inverse projection, $1\otimes F_fh$, the counit, and $D_YN\otimes N\to\omega_Y$. Pullback adjunction transposes the first arrow and the internal adjunction transposes the last two, so this is precisely postcomposition with $\theta_N$. Yoneda makes $\theta_N$ an isomorphism at every finite level. The section comparison detects equivalences by evaluations, and the duality/site comparisons identify the resulting map with the canonical finite exceptional isomorphism. The tensor-Hom construction also gives its evaluation and transpose identities before any inverse limit.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-3: explicit tensor-Hom/counit construction of the finite dual formula.

proof.text: For normalized $M,N$, the mapping-complex clause of [lem-coef-cartesian-section-adjoint-mates] gives the actual coherent-system transpose $h\mapsto\mathcal E_f(h)\circ\eta_M$ and inverse $g\mapsto\epsilon_N\circ\mathcal F_f(g)$. The system tensor-Hom calculus identifies these mapping systems with the stated $\mathcal H_Y$ and $\mathcal H_X$, and the section triangle identities make the composites identities before total inverse limit.

source.place: Paragraph 2: enriched mapping-complex adjunction, with explicit inverse before $R\lim$.

proof.text:
At level $n$, the transpose is the canonical enriched étale adjunction: [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] identifies $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(M,f^	imes N)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(Rf_!M,N)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies derived direct-image composition with global sections. The compact-support and site comparisons [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identify these maps and their counits with the finite pro-étale maps. On mapping complexes: for étale-origin $K$ finite-Tor constructible and $L$ bounded constructible, [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] gives $
u^*R\mathcal Hom(K,L)\cong R\mathcal Hom(
u^*K,
u^*L)$; since $R\mathcal Hom(K,L)$ is bounded below, the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $\Gamma_{\mathrm{proet}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{et}}\circ
u_*$ give $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{proet}}(
u^*K,
u^*L)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{et}}(K,L)$. This applies to both sides, with $(Rf_{!,n}M_n,N_n)$ and $(M_n,Rf_n^!N_n)$ in these domains by steps 2 and 3. The hypotheses hold because $A_n$ is a finite quotient of the valuation ring of a finite local-field extension ([lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]), $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and the compactification is open followed by proper finite type. Inputs are bounded and of étale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. The finite exceptional unit/counit identities then identify the maps with those specified in [lem-coef-finite-exceptional].

source.place: Paragraph 2, enriched adjunction transported from the étale site; paragraph 3, units/counits.

proof.text: For integral inputs whose reductions lie in $\mathscr N_X$, let $\rho_{m,n}:M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n$ be the strict transition and let $c_{m,n}:F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_n$ be [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. The output transition is $F_mM_m\to F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_nM_n$. Its scalar-extension adjoint is $Q_YF_mM_m\to F_nQ_XM_m\to F_nM_n$, because $c_{m,n}$ and its mate are both the counit transpose on the simultaneous models. Thus it is exactly the transition of step 2 and of the definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Applying $\mathcal L_Y=R\lim\circ U_Y$ gives $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ with the specified finite projections; step 4 supplies the dualizing total-limit identification.

source.place: Paragraph 2, finite compact-support tower before $R\lim$, and last paragraph, dualizing total limit.
